claims.text: Controlled build-chamber preheating during SLM/PBF-LB of high-entropy alloys reduces thermal gradients during solidification.
Reducing solidification thermal gradients through preheating improves dimensional precision.
Reducing solidification thermal gradients through preheating improves mechanical integrity by minimizing fabrication-induced defects.
As-built HEA components made without chamber preheating typically have elevated residual stresses and dimensional inaccuracies.
As-built HEA components made without chamber preheating typically have more porosity and micro-cracking.
The useful chamber-preheating temperature is below the alloy solidus but high enough to moderate thermal gradients.
Equiatomic CoCrFeNiMn can be fabricated by SLM into components with complex geometries.
Chamber preheating produces a more uniform temperature distribution during layer deposition.
The more uniform temperature distribution reduces rapid cooling and thermal gradients.
The altered thermal history promotes more uniform grain growth.
The altered thermal history decreases porosity, micro-cracking, and residual stress.
Slower cooling caused by preheating minimizes thermally induced stresses.
Preheating produces a more homogeneous microstructure with fewer fabrication-induced defects.
Preheated samples will have tighter dimensional tolerances than otherwise identical samples made without preheating.
Preheated samples will have lower porosity and fewer micro-cracks than samples made without preheating.
Preheated samples will have greater tensile strength than samples made without preheating.
Preheated samples will have greater ductility than samples made without preheating.
The intervention should apply to HEAs with composition and melting behavior similar to CoCrFeNiMn under conventional SLM/PBF-LB conditions.
The effectiveness of chamber preheating may vary with alloy thermal properties and with pre-existing thermal-management strategies.
